data.hypothesis: The per-pixel turbulence work is likely dominated by repeated gradient evaluation and dependent NoisePerm lookups. Compiler-generated SIMD variants across adjacent x pixels may overlap independent lanes while preserving each pixel's math, but dependent gathers may be costly or scalarized; full-call speedup is uncertain. Let the compiler choose vector width and tail handling, and measure against the valid baseline.
data.notes: This is the first, compiler-directed SIMD variant: it adds OpenMP SIMD function variants and maps the row's adjacent pixels to SIMD lanes, without changing formulas or adding explicit ISA intrinsics. It is intended to expose the cost of compiler-generated dependent permutation-table accesses; an explicit-intrinsic implementation remains a separate comparison. The supplied baseline is valid with mean 0.3109329016666666 seconds over three samples, but this candidate has not been measured. Exact build flags were not supplied, so SIMD enablement and performance must be determined by the controller. The inner loop covers all widths without an assumed vector multiple.
transformations: Added OpenMP declare simd variants for the active scalar helpers and kernels, marking only known uniform coordinates/parameters as uniform.
Added an OpenMP simd directive to the adjacent-pixel inner loop, leaving vector width and tail handling to the compiler.
Preserved the per-pixel noise and turbulence computation order and formulas; made no explicit-intrinsic or algorithmic rewrite.
